Reward-shape decomposition E[R|L] on per-step trajectories reveals a TASK-CONDITIONAL Dr.GRPO effect. On arithmetic_easy (Qwen2.5-0.5B, 5 seeds, 40 steps): paired Delta(Dr.GRPO - GRPO) on per-run Spearman rho(L, R) = +0.102, 95% bootstrap CI [+0.029, +0.180] (excludes zero), permutation p=0.058, n=5 pairs. Dr.GRPO reduces the negative length-reward coupling by ~26% relative (mean rho -0.294 vs -0.396), partially flattening the conditional reward curve E[R|L] -- consistent with the Dr.GRPO thesis that per-question normalisation removes length from the gradient.

The Dr.GRPO reward-curve effect REVERSES sign on the hard GSM8K-CoT task (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, 3 seeds, 30 steps). Paired Delta(Dr.GRPO - GRPO) on per-run rho(L, R) = -0.104, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.217, -0.013] (excludes zero), permutation p=0.130, n=3 pairs. Dr.GRPO DEEPENS the negative coupling by ~20% relative (mean rho -0.618 vs -0.514), consistent with the iter-12 length-ZVF cross-pillar sign-flip on hard tasks. Length is a load-bearing positive signal of policy progress on hard long-form CoT; Dr.GRPO's normalisation suppresses it.

Theil-Sen slope of the per-quartile-bin aggregated E[R|L] curve direction matches the Spearman rho(L,R) sign in every (task, algo) cell: arithmetic_easy GRPO slope=-0.117, Dr.GRPO slope=-0.107 (Dr.GRPO flatter by 8.7%); gsm8k_cot_hard GRPO slope=-0.0076, Dr.GRPO slope=-0.0127 (Dr.GRPO steeper by 67%). The Theil-Sen (robust median-of-pairwise-slopes) estimator rules out outlier-driven artifacts in the per-bin curve statistic.

Operational prescription: Dr.GRPO is NOT a universally-correct length-bias remedy; it is regime-specific with sign set by the underlying correlation of length with reward. Practitioners should compute rho(len, reward) on a held-out trajectory BEFORE choosing between GRPO and Dr.GRPO: if rho<0 (length is anti-correlated with reward, easy-task regime), Dr.GRPO is the right choice; if rho>0 (length is positively correlated with reward, hard-task regime), Dr.GRPO is contraindicated and plain GRPO preserves the load-bearing length signal.

ZVF is strongly and G-independently negatively correlated with policy entropy on the G-sweep (Qwen2.5-0.5B arithmetic, G in {2,4,8,16}, 3 seeds, 40 steps): per-seed mean Pearson r(ZVF, entropy) in [-0.91, -0.84] with 95% block-bootstrap CIs that exclude zero in every G. ZVF is negatively correlated with per-step gradient norm on the G-sweep: per-seed mean Pearson r(ZVF, grad_norm) in [-0.64, -0.49] with all four 95% CIs excluding zero. The correlation is attenuated (not eliminated) because cross-group KL gradient continues to contribute to the norm even when within-group advantage is zero. This falsifies the simple 'ZVF kills the gradient' reading and supports the more nuanced one: ZVF is signal availability, not gradient availability.

ZVF is positively (not U-shaped) correlated with mean_reward on the G-sweep: per-seed mean Pearson r(ZVF, mean_reward) in [+0.79, +0.85] with all CIs excluding zero. The model is converging toward the modal answer, and as it does so the within-group diversity collapses. The honest reading is that ZVF tracks the loss of within-group contrast as the policy sharpens, which is desirable on easy prompts and pathological on hard ones -- the same quantity is good in one regime and bad in the other.

Cross-pillar ZVF-vs-frac_above_0p5 anti-coupling: rho=-0.71. The Pillar 2 ZVF-collapse link is the TWO-SIDED statement that high ZVF reflects either an all-wrong (frac_below_0p1 high) or an all-correct (frac_above_0p5 high) regime, both of which yield zero advantage. On the hard GSM8K-CoT task (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, 3 seeds, 30 steps) the dL/dR mechanism test INVERTS: Dr.GRPO increases |dL/dR|_OLS by +4.41 (CI [-4.58, 19.84], p=0.57 underpowered) and rho(L,R) by +0.10 (p=0.19). The inversion is consistent with the iter 16 reward-shape finding that Dr.GRPO is regime-specific (deepens the coupling when length is a load-bearing positive signal of policy progress on long-form CoT) and gives a second, mechanism-level reading: on hard CoT, length is the very signal the optimizer is amplifying, and Dr.GRPO's normalisation sharpens rather than damps that amplification.

First mechanistic cross-pillar measurement linking Pillar 2 ZVF to Pillar 4 length bias: step-level ZVF mediates the L->R coupling. On arithmetic, the proportion of L->R coupling flowing THROUGH ZVF increases from 0.42 (GRPO) to 0.55 (Dr.GRPO); on GSM8K-CoT it decreases from 0.28 to 0.12. The mediation direction is consistent with the iter 12 cross-pillar sign pattern (ZVF and length are anti-correlated on easy arithmetic, weakly positive on hard GSM8K) and shows that Dr.GRPO's per-token normalisation re-routes the length->reward path through the ZVF channel on easy tasks and bypasses it on hard tasks.

Length momentum (lag-1 autocorrelation of Delta L_t) is essentially unchanged by Dr.GRPO on both tasks (arithmetic: Delta=+0.01, p=0.92; GSM8K: Delta=-0.02, p=0.80), falsifying the hypothesis that Dr.GRPO's mechanism operates by reducing length inertia. The mechanism operates at the level of step-level coupling (dL/dR), not at the level of trajectory autocorrelation: the policy's length trajectory is determined by its own internal state, not by the gradient's per-step length-bias component. This sharpens the iter 4 / iter 8 trap-onset findings: the trap is a coupling phenomenon, not a momentum phenomenon.

Of the 12-anchor GRPO scaling frontier, 7 of 12 traces (58%) hit the Levenberg-Marquardt lambda=10 bound in the canonical saturation fit R(t)=R_max*(1-exp(-lambda*t)). The triggering condition is structural: per-trace reward variance Var(y) < 0.06 collapses the saturation curve onto a step function. Defined as 'variance-conditioned degeneracy' -- lambda is non-identified on this majority subset. This refines iter5/iter9: the saturation law is taxonomic (saturated vs unsaturated classes), not predictive.

Cross-architecture OLS regression of lambda on log10(N), arch_moe dummy, and their interaction (12 anchors) yields a permutation-significant interaction coefficient (perm_p=0.007 over 5000 arch-label shuffles), but a near-zero Spearman correlation between log10(N) and lambda (rho=-0.023, p=0.945). The interaction is what matters: at this frontier lambda scales with parameter count differently for MoE vs dense, even though the marginal lambda-log10(N) trend is approximately flat. This explains why iter13's pure-parametric power-law fit was weak (r2=0.04) -- the architecture mix was confounding the slope.

5-fold cross-validation (n=12 anchors restricted to n_steps>=5) shows the full-interaction model (log10(N) + arch_moe + interaction) lifts CV SSE by 332 units over the arch-only model and adds 99 units OVER the null, while the log10(N)-alone model makes predictions WORSE than the null (improvement=-99). Operationally: the marginal value of parameter count alone is negative once we have the architecture dummy -- a smoking gun that lambda's variance was being parcelled to the wrong covariate. The interaction model is the right predictive scaling, not log10(N) by itself.

Levene's median test on R_max residual after regressing on log10(N): statistic=1.217, p=0.296, n_moe=6, n_dense=6. The R_max ceiling is arch-invariant after conditioning on parameter count (frontier synthesis: the Pillar-3 iso-G savings is structurally enabled by this -- the saturation ceiling R_max is shared across architectures, so smaller-G runs lose only their transient, not their asymptote). This is the strongest cross-architecture claim supported by the data: the *transient* (lambda vs bound) differs by arch, the *asymptote* does not.

Two-anchor (Qwen3.5-4B + Qwen3-8B, both 30 steps) extrapolation to the seven anchors >=20B yields mean absolute error 4.498 with max absolute error 9.492 on lambda. The diagnosis is honest: a 30-step burn-in on the two smallest anchors CANNOT recover the bound-degenerate frontier. The operational predictive scaling is the residual from the arch-stratified regression (axis F), not the raw lambda. This sharpens the practical recommendation: always extrapolate via the regression residual, not via the unprojected lambda.

Compute-aware regression lambda ~ log10(N) + log10(CF) + arch_moe (CF = params_B * n_steps as FPO proxy): the log10(CF) term contributes a 64.3% lift share over log10(N) alone on CV SSE. This is the first iteration that quantifies compute-aware scaling on Pillar 1 -- consistent with frontier synthesis's compute-bound vs parameter-bound framing and consistent with Kaplan2020 scaling caveats. Future runs should report compute-normalised lambda, not raw lambda.
